fields.why: NSCPS is a weighted, nationally representative CDC survey of U.S. K-12 public schools, so 'national survey' fits best, though the brief's national-survey list names only person-level surveys (NHIS, BRFSS, ...), leaving 'other survey' defensible.

V15(d)/brief exclude 'rurality of non-human units', but schools are groups of people (the brief's own ecologic example) and the article frames rural schools' shortfall as an equity concern; B's literal reading is defensible. Age (K-12) as population follows 'recorded always'.
If school locale is rurality, Table 2 notes cover all six locale pairs by chi-square, a pairwise (all pairs) entry with 4 groups, as A recorded; it hinges on the same rurality rule.
Locale is both a compared variable (Table 2) and a sampling stratum (sampling-design strata on an SPD get role covariate); depends on accepting school rurality as an SPD.

brief_issues: Rurality rule (V15(d), 'non-human units') does not say whether institutions serving people (schools, clinics) count; proposed: rurality of institutions that stand for the people they serve is an SPD. National-survey list could say whether nationally representative facility/school surveys count.
